subject: General Aptitude
summary: permutations and combinations (repeated letters, restrictions, circular arrangements, selections), basic and conditional probability (addition rule, independent events, Bayes), mensuration of plane figures and solids, and reading tables, bar, line and pie charts

questions.text: The number of distinct arrangements of all the letters of the word BANANA is
solution: Concept: n objects with groups of identical ones: n!/(p! q! …).
BANANA has 6 letters: A three times, N twice, B once.
Exam tip: Count the repeats carefully before dividing; a missed repeat doubles or triples the answer.

questions.text: A committee of 4 is to be chosen from 6 men and 5 women so that it has at least 2 women. The number of ways is ______
solution: Concept: 'At least' problems: add the separate exact cases (or subtract the unwanted cases from the total).
Exam tip: Never fix 2 women first and then choose 'any 2 of the rest': that counts the same committee several times.

questions.text: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is a king or a heart is
solution: Concept: Addition rule: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
Exam tip: Option (A) 17/52 is the trap answer that forgets to remove the king of hearts counted twice.

questions.text: Two fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers is a prime number (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: List the favourable sums and count the outcomes for each.
Exam tip: Ways to get sum s with two dice = 6 − |s − 7| for s = 2 to 12.

questions.text: A rectangular garden 60 m × 40 m has a path 2 m wide running all round it on the outside. The area of the path is
solution: Concept: Path area = outer rectangle − inner rectangle.
Exam tip: For a path of width w outside, each dimension grows by 2w; inside, each shrinks by 2w (giving 384 m² here: option C).

questions.text: A solid metal sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and drawn into a uniform wire of radius 1 mm. The length of the wire (in m) is ______
solution: Concept: Volume is conserved when a solid is melted and recast.
Exam tip: Convert every length to the same unit (here cm) before equating volumes.

questions.text: The bar chart shows the profit of a company from 2020 to 2024. The profit in 2024 is about what percentage more than the average profit of the five years?
solution: Concept: Percentage more = (value − base)/base × 100, with the average as the base.
Exam tip: 25 % is the rise over 2023 only; read which base the question asks for.

questions.text: The pie chart shows the monthly budget of a family as central angles. By how many rupees per month do the savings exceed the transport spending? ______
solution: Exam tip: Work with the difference of angles first; one multiplication then gives the answer.

questions.text: The line graph shows the output of two plants A and B. In which year did plant A's output exceed plant B's by the largest percentage (of B's output)?
solution: Concept: Percentage excess = (A − B)/B × 100; a large absolute gap need not be a large percentage gap.
Exam tip: The biggest absolute gaps (2021 and 2024, 6 thousand tonnes) are the traps here.

questions.text: The table shows the marks of five students. The average total marks (out of 300) of the students who scored more than 75 in Physics is ______
solution: Concept: Filter the rows first, then average the required quantity.
Exam tip: Divya scored 74 in Physics, so she is just excluded: read the cut-off ('more than') carefully.

questions.text: A bag has 3 white and 2 black balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other with replacement. The probability that one is white and the other is black is
solution: Concept: With replacement, the draws are independent; the two orders (WB and BW) are separate cases.
Exam tip: Without replacement the answer would be 2 × (3/5)(2/4) = 3/5 (option D).

questions.text: The number of ways of distributing 6 different books among 3 students so that each student gets exactly 2 books is ______
solution: Concept: Distributing distinct objects into labelled groups of fixed sizes: n!/(n₁! n₂! n₃!).
First student: C(6,2) = 15; second: C(4,2) = 6; third: C(2,2) = 1
Exam tip: If the groups were unlabelled (just three piles), divide by 3! to get 15.

questions.text: The radius of a right circular cylinder is doubled and its height is halved. Its volume
solution: Exam tip: The curved surface area 2πrh stays the same in this case: (2r)(h/2) = rh.

questions.text: Machine M1 makes 60 % of a factory's output with 2 % defectives, and machine M2 makes the rest with 5 % defectives. An item picked at random is found to be defective. The probability that it was made by M2 (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Bayes' theorem: P(M2 | D) = P(M2)P(D | M2)/P(D).
Exam tip: A tree with the joint probabilities (0.012 and 0.020) makes Bayes problems one division.

questions.text: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. Its area is about
solution: Concept: Area of an equilateral triangle of side a = (√3/4)a².
Exam tip: Its height is (√3/2)a = 10.39 cm; ½ × base × height gives the same area as a check.
